analyst_view.overall: Early view: promoted Racing, coached by José Alberto, have the league's worst defence (30 conceded in 12) and are without Mantilla (cruciate) and Andrés Martín (muscle). Real Sociedad (5th) have confirmed Ander Barrenetxea suffered a severe hamstring injury against Rayo that needs surgery and could keep him out for much of the season, and Sucic is also out. La Real's away games have been wide open, 13 scored and 13 conceded in six.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I have moved from lower to the site's view. Losing Barrenetxea and Sucic blunts La Real, but Racing concede 2.5 a game, Racing's home games have averaged nearly four goals and La Real's away games over four, so I no longer see a reason to go below the numbers.

corners.text: The site expects 11.3 corners. Racing average about five corners a game, and La Real lose Barrenetxea, one of the wingers who drives play to the byline. Ten or 11 is more realistic than 12.

cards.text: The model has 5.2 cards. Racing have 31 yellows in 12 games and La Real 24 yellows and three reds, so both sit close to average and nothing points clearly either way until the referee is named.

shots.text: The site expects 31.3 shots. Racing average about 12 shots a game and La Real had 17 at home to Rayo, which adds up to the high 20s rather than over 30. A tired La Real without Barrenetxea and Sucic, with a Europa League trip four days later, also points down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 on target. Racing put about 4.5 a game on target, and La Real lose two creators in Barrenetxea and Sucic. Expect about 9, even in an open game.
